Diego M: Hey support — since ~10:30 UTC our app started returning a mix of 502s and occasional 401s, and EU customers see very high p95. We noticed automatic fallback to us-east during the window which doubled latency and caused a billing spike. Example request id: abc123. Any quick diagnostics?

Alice S: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used and the X-Request-ID? Also which region are you pinning in the client?

Diego M: Here is a minimal repro I used: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: abc123" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-v2"
```
Response snippet: `{"error":"fallback: routed to us-east-1","status":502,"server":"hotshard-42"}`

Ben R: I can see eu-west pool spiking around that time — an overloaded hotshard caused queue_depth to climb. Routing policy auto-spillover routed traffic to us-east (makes sense) which explains the latency. The 401s are odd — likely token scoping interacting with fallback (token checks sometimes differ by deployment). Do you set any sticky routing header?

Diego M: Token is org-scoped as far as we know. We do explicitly set `X-Client-Region`. We also saw billing jump in the same 15m window; we have 500 reserved capacity so curious why fallback fired early.

Clara P: What were the autoscaler and queue metrics at the time? If autoscale lagged, fallback could trigger sooner. Ben, can you pull routing logs for abc123?

Ben R: Quick grep: 
`2026-11-18T10:31:05Z route decision: eu-west pool overloaded -> fallback(us-east, reason=queue_depth>1000, spillover_count=27) request=abc123`
Also: `token-scope-check: warn: token-region-mismatch: none` (so token wasn't region-scoped).

Alice S: Diego, can you try forcing the region in a repro with `X-Force-Region: eu-west-1` and include `X-Client-Request-ID` so we can correlate? A HAR would help too.

Diego M: Doing a quick loop; reproduced the 401s after fallback. Steps: 
1) 10:30 send 20 concurrent requests with `X-Client-Region: eu-west-1`
2) ~3/20 get 401 with body `{"code":"auth.region_mismatch"}` when those requests hit us-east fallback
3) 5-10s later some requests succeed

Repro loop: 
```
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-...' -H 'X-Client-Region: eu-west-1' -H "X-Client-Request-ID: repro-$i" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

Nila B: Billing saw ~2.3x token usage billed for that org between 10:30-10:45 UTC. If compute executed in another region that's billed normally. I'll open a billing ticket, but need the list of request IDs to reconcile. @Diego M can you paste the repro IDs when you have them?

Ben R: Root cause hypothesis: an uneven hot-shard (hotshard-42) degraded (GPU memory thrash) leading to queue buildup. The routing spillover threshold is 500 in config but we saw a race where a circuit-breaker triggered fallback early due to a transient metric spike. Two related bugs: (1) fallback logic didn't re-check token validity for the target region before routing, so some fallback requests hit auth guards and returned 401; (2) autoscaler delay allowed queue to grow before replicas added.

Short-term mitigations: 
- You can pin the org to eu-west via account flag `routing.pin.region=eu-west-1` (temporary).
- We can disable autospillover for your org `routing.autospillover=false` while we fix.
- We'll drain hotshard-42 and scale the pool.

Clara P: Action items: Ben to provide full list of affected request IDs + timeline; eng-infra to investigate hotshard kernel/GPU errors and drain; support to get customer to pin region / disable autospillover; billing to prepare provisional credit if usage is clearly unexpected. Ben ETA?

Ben R: I can drain and scale within ~30m. Will attach logs and request id list here. Marking this P2. infra-bot: starting drain job for hotshard-42.

infra-bot: drain-job drain-1863: started. progress: 0/24 replicas moved.

Diego M: Thanks — we've enabled `routing.pin.region=eu-west-1` and turned off autospillover. I'll post the repro IDs in #support-tickets once the loop finishes. Please hold on billing until we share the list.

Alice S: Appreciate the quick coordination. We'll follow up with a short incident timeline and postmortem once we confirm root cause. :bow:
